title: C-level readout playbook + customer quarterly recap email
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook is a lightweight, repeatable template for a C-level (CEO/CRO/CPO) readout and an accompanying customer-facing quarterly recap email. The goal: make the sponsor feel briefed on outcomes, risks, and asks in under 5 minutes while leaving room for a short advisory convo.

Status notes:
- Draft: needs review from AE + SE for customer-specific numbers.
- Use "one-pager" section to generate the slide-first agenda for exec meetings.
- Keep all public-facing language non-technical; attach technical appendix when needed.

WHEN TO USE
- Quarterly business review with exec sponsor (formal cadence)
- Mid-cycle renewal signal (60–90 days before renewal)
- Post-major-implementation milestone where executive endorsement unlocks budget

1) Quick reference: 2-slide/e-mail-first variants
- Two-minute executive summary (email subject + 3 bullets): ideal for CEO/CRO inbox
- One-pager for the sponsor deck (single slide content + 3 visuals: ARR impact, SLA trend, Roadmap alignment)
- Optional: 5-min follow-up call with 2 ask points

Email subject line options (pick 1):
- "Quarterly readout & top asks — [Customer] x Redwood"
- "[Customer] Q1 outcomes + recommended next steps"
- "Highlights + ask: Redwood & [Customer] — Qtr recap"

Email: Two-minute summary (concise)
Subject: [pick above]
Hi [Sponsor first name],

Quick Q1 recap for [Customer] + two short asks.
- Outcomes: 1) Reduced inference cost per 1k tokens by 22% via batching + quantization pilot; 2) Average P95 latency improved from 420ms -> 310ms on highest-volume route; 3) Feature adoption: 5 product teams shipping with Redwood in production.
- Risk: Model drift observed on the search reranker for 2 queries (low volume) — SE suggested profiling and prompt-set retest this month.
- Asks: 1) Approve 12% reserved capacity commit for Q3 to guarantee latency SLO for holiday spike; 2) Exec intro to platform infra team to discuss private deployment timeline.

Can we schedule a 15-min touchpoint next week to align on the asks?
Thanks,
Maya Thompson

Email: Longer recap (customer-facing, with metrics + next steps)
Subject: [Customer] — Q1 business recap, risks, and recommended asks
Hi [Sponsor first name] and team,

Thanks for partnering with us this quarter. Below is a short recap of what moved the needle and where we need your support.

Headline outcomes:
- Cost: Token cost/unit down 22% (pilot); projected run-rate savings: $48k/mo once pilot scales; verification plan attached.
- Performance: P50/P95 latency trend improved across primary routes (P95 now 310ms, down 26%); availability 99.92% this quarter.
- Adoption: 5 product squads are live; daily traffic up 3.6x for the primary route.

Business impact narrative (1–2 sentences):
Redwood improvements shortened user task completion time by ~1.2s on average and reduced inference spend for the targeted flow, improving margin on the A/B tested feature.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Model quality regression on search reranker for niche queries. Mitigation: SE will run a focused eval and deploy a prompt-set fix by 2025-02-10. Owner: Rina Kapoor.
- Risk: Capacity exposure during Black Friday window if no reserved commit. Mitigation: Approve 12% reserved capacity commit or allow burst policy to extend for the month of Nov. Owner: Daniel Park.

Recommended asks (clear, single-sentence asks to send to exec):
1) Approve 12% reserved capacity commitment starting 2025-10-01 (business justification: guarantee P95 < 350ms for priority routes during expected traffic surge)
2) Introduce Redwood CS lead to [Customer] platform infra lead by 2025-02-15 to align on private deployment prerequisites

KPIs / Metrics table (paste into slide)
- Total inference cost change (QoQ): -22%
- P95 latency (primary): 310ms (was 420ms)
- Availability (platform): 99.92%
- Active product squads: 5
- Projected monthly savings at scale: $48,000

One-pager / slide content (single slide)
- Header: [Customer] + Redwood — Q1 Executive Readout
- Left column: 'Top outcomes' bullets (as above) + small 3-line business impact statement
- Middle: 2 charts (cost trend, latency trend) — include alt text in email for accessibility
- Right column: 'Top risks' and 'Asks' with owners and target dates
- Footer: next step (15-min alignment call) + contact info (Maya Thompson, CS lead)

Meeting agenda (15 min)
1) 0:00–0:03 — One-line summary + sentiment (green/amber/red)
2) 0:03–0:07 — Outcomes + metrics (visuals)
3) 0:07–0:11 — Risks + proposed mitigation (ask focus)
4) 0:11–0:15 — Confirm decisions, owners, and timeframe

Talking points for sponsor (short, use cue-phrases)
- "We reduced run-rate inference spend while improving latency on the top route — that directly improves margin on Feature X."
- "We need a short exec OK on reserved capacity to assure SLOs for the holiday window."
- "If you can introduce us to the infra lead, we'll handle the private deployment checklist and timeline."

Customer-facing quarterly recap email sample (full)
Subject: [Customer] Q1 recap: outcomes, risks & two requests
Hi [Sponsor first name],

Appreciate your time — below is a brief summary of Q1 and two small asks to keep momentum.
OUTCOMES
- 22% lower inference cost per targeted flow (pilot to run scale)
- P95 latency improved 26% (420ms -> 310ms)
- 5 product squads live with Redwood; adoption increasing
RISKS
- Minor model quality drift on low-volume queries; SE will run a retest and propose fixes by 2025-02-10
REQUESTS
1) Approve 12% reserved capacity commit for Q3 to secure latency SLOs during expected spikes
2) Exec intro to [Customer] infra lead to discuss private deployment prerequisites

Would love to grab 15 minutes next week to confirm next steps — what time works best?
Best,
Maya

Appendix: Technical backing (attach as PDF or as Google doc link)
- Pilot methodology and sample size
- Eval results for reranker (before/after)
- Cost model & assumptions

Internal checklist before sending
- [ ] Confirm cost projection with finance (Danita)
- [ ] Verify P95 numbers with SRE metrics dashboard (Leo)
- [ ] Attach technical appendix (Rina)
- [ ] Localize any legal/compliance phrasing if private deployment discussion will include data residency

Decision flow & owners (short)
- Sponsor approval (exec): sign-off on asks -> AE captures commitment in contract amendment (owner: Daniel Park)
- SE/SRE: validate mitigations and ETA (owner: Rina / Leo)
- CS: follow-up comms + schedule technical alignment (owner: Maya)

Unresolved questions / TODOs (working section)
- Confirm renewal window date (we have conflicting dates in Contract doc; need AE confirmation)
- Clarify whether burst capacity can be purchased ad-hoc during holiday period vs reserved commit (ops team to confirm)
- Draft legal-friendly wording for reserved capacity amendment (legal review needed)

Quick templates for on-call follow-up Slack/Email (copy/paste)
Slack (to infra lead): "Hi [Name], Maya from Redwood here — looking to sync on a 20-min runbook to prep private deployment. Are you available this or next Tues?"
Email (to sponsor after meeting): "Thanks for your time — per our convo: you approved the 12% reserve and agreed to intro us to infra lead. AE to send amendment and intro by EOD 2025-02-05."

Versioning / notes
- 0.1 (2025-01-10): initial draft
- 0.2 (2025-02-03): added metrics, appendix checklist, aligned owners

Delivery notes (best practices)
- Send the concise email to sponsor at start-of-week (Mon/Tues) with slide-first one-pager attached; copy AE + SE.
- Always include a single clear ask (approval + intro) — executives rarely action multiple asks without a follow-up.
- Use the one-pager slide as the primary visuals in the calendar invite; keep meeting to 15 minutes.

Attachments to prepare (links/placeholders)
- Slide: [link to deck placeholder]
- Technical appendix: [link to doc placeholder]
- Cost model spreadsheet: [link to sheet placeholder]

Notes to self: keep language outcome-driven, no model internals in the initial email, include technical appendix for the infra/SE audience only.
